title: 1 · The 28 letters, family by family
blurb: Name and sound the Arabic letters, tell look-alikes apart by their dots, and read your first words.

title: 2 · Throat and heavy sounds
blurb: Hear and roughly say the Arabic sounds English lacks, and tell word pairs like heart and dog apart.

title: 3 · Short and long vowels
blurb: Read the three short vowel marks and the three long vowels, and hear why length changes a word.

title: 4 · Joining letters: start, middle, end
blurb: Find a letter at the start, middle and end of a word, and spot the six letters that never join forward.

title: 5 · Sukun and shadda
blurb: Read sukun (no vowel), shadda (a doubled letter) and the gliding vowels aw and ay.

title: 6 · Hamza, alif maqsura and tanwin
blurb: Read hamza on its seats, ى at the end of a word, ة, and the -an ending of words like شُكْرًا.

title: 7 · ال: the article, sun and moon letters
blurb: Say "the" in Arabic, hear when its l disappears, and tell "the big house" from "The house is big."

title: 8 · Greetings and goodbyes
blurb: Greet anyone at any time of day, ask how someone is (to a man or to a woman), thank, apologize and say goodbye.

title: 9 · Masculine and feminine: ة
blurb: Tell masculine from feminine words, choose the right "this" and "it", and make a describing word agree.

title: 10 · I, you, he, she
blurb: Say I, you (to a man or to a woman), he, she, it, we and they, and make the word after them agree.

title: 11 · Sentences with no "is"
blurb: Say who you are and what things are like with two words and no verb: أَنَا طَالِب, الْبَيْت كَبِير.

title: 12 · "The" and "a": ال and no ال
blurb: Know when a noun needs ال, when it needs nothing, and how one ال turns a sentence into a phrase.

title: 13 · Where you're from: -ī and -iyya
blurb: Say where you and others are from, and turn any country into "American", "Egyptian" or "Moroccan" for a man or a woman.

title: 14 · Question words: ما, من, أين, هل
blurb: Ask what, who, where, how, when and how many, and turn any sentence into a yes / no question with هَل.

title: 15 · Numbers 0 to 100
blurb: Count from 0 to 100, read the digits used in much of the Arab world, and say a price.

title: 16 · Ordering and paying
blurb: Order in a café, ask what something costs, and ask for the check, to a man or a woman.

title: 17 · Noun + adjective: agreement
blurb: Describe anything with one or two adjectives that follow the noun and agree with it in gender and in "the".

title: 18 · Iḍāfa: the X of Y
blurb: Join two nouns to say "the student's book", "the door of the house" or "the train station".

title: 19 · My, your, his, her: possessive endings
blurb: Say my, your, his, her and our with an ending on the noun: بَيْتِي, اِسْمُكَ, بَيْتُهَا.

title: 20 · عند: to have
blurb: Say what you, he, she and we have, ask "Do you have…?", and say "I don't have".

title: 21 · Plurals: sound and broken
blurb: Make plurals with -ūn and -āt, recognize broken plurals, and describe plural things with a feminine adjective.

title: 22 · Roots and patterns
blurb: Spot the three-letter root inside a word, guess what a pattern adds, and find a word in a dictionary.

title: 23 · Present-tense verbs
blurb: Say what you, he, she, we and they do every day with one set of prefixes and endings.

title: 24 · Verb sentences and word order
blurb: Start a sentence with the verb or with the subject, and keep the verb agreeing either way.

title: 25 · Saying no: لا and ليس
blurb: Say "not" the Arabic way: one word before a verb, another before a place, an adjective or "I have".

title: 26 · Time words and adverbs
blurb: Say when and how often: today, now, every day, in the evening, the days of the week, and "very".

title: 27 · Past-tense verbs
blurb: Say what you, he, she, we and they did, with one set of endings on the verb.

title: 28 · Asking for help and directions
blurb: Stop someone politely, ask where a place is, and understand right, left, straight ahead, near and far.
